title: Pedalling, and the ear that hears the blur
summary: Learn to hear the moment the pedal blurs one chord into the next, and lift it before it does.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: A bar of four beats: a chord struck on beat one and held through beat two, then struck again exactly on beat three and held through beat four. This is the precise lift and press of the pedal at each chord change, instead of a blur across it.

steps.title: Pedalling, and the ear that hears the blur
steps.body:
The right pedal lifts every damper at once, so the strings keep ringing after your fingers let go. Held too long across a chord change, the old chord rings into the new one and the sound turns to mud. The fix is not less pedal. It is better timing.

1. Play a chord, press the pedal down, hold it, then change to the next chord without moving the pedal. Listen to the blur.
2. Now change the pedal exactly at the chord change: lift it and press again in one quick motion, right as the new chord lands.
3. Practise that lift-and-press at every chord change in the hard bars, slowly, until it feels automatic.
4. Play the whole piece with the pedal changing at each chord change, listening for a clean sound instead of a blur.

Your foot has a job as precise as your fingers. It just has fewer notes to learn.

figure.alt: The same lift-and-press bar: a chord held, then struck and held again exactly on the next chord change, practised slowly at every chord change in the hard bars.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: hold the pedal across a chord change on purpose, and listen to the blur
Sitting 2: lift-and-press at each chord change in the hard bars, slowly, five times
Sitting 3: the same lift-and-press, one notch faster, then once through
Sitting 4: the whole piece with clean pedal changes, then once as if recording
An old piece played once, listening only to the pedal

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Say the name of the piece, then play it once through with the pedal, hands in the frame.
